sections.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
sections.abstract: MindTopo introduces an 11,030-instance benchmark covering continuity, separation, order, enclosure, and knots, testing multimodal models on both topological reasoning and closed-loop planning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a topology-grounded benchmark and report a large reasoning-versus-planning gap.
sections.caveat: Generated rollouts do not reliably preserve environment dynamics and topology; results are preliminary.

sections.title: COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization
sections.abstract: COBRA-Skills treats reusable-agent-skill improvement as budgeted sequential optimization, combining contextual-bandit prioritization with evidence-grounded evolution.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports strongest average performance among compared methods while reducing optimization cost by 55–58% versus SkillOpt.
sections.caveat: Evidence is limited to selected benchmarks and baselines.

sections.title: When Agents Disagree: Bayesian Backward Reasoning as a Label-Free Anchor for Multi-Agent Collective Decision-Making
sections.abstract: This work uses reverse Bayesian posteriors and Jensen–Shannon cross-path consistency to aggregate conflicting LLM-agent answers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report gains from MinJS, FwdJS, and LogLin, especially on disagreement cases.
sections.caveat: Evidence is centered on one diagnostic benchmark.

sections.title: From Parameters to Answers: How LLMs Retrieve and Use Their Internal Knowledge
sections.abstract: Layerwise hidden-state interventions across Qwen, Llama, and Gemma separate query-routing signals from answer-supporting content.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report distinct layerwise routing and content trajectories across models and protocols.
sections.caveat: The controlled tasks do not yet establish generalization to broad knowledge retrieval.

sections.title: Artificial Id: Drive and Persistent Alignment in Agentic AI
sections.abstract: The paper proposes an internal adaptive drive for deciding whether an agent should continue, stop, or change behavior.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author frames alignment as a property of a continuing agentic system with persistent state and authority boundaries.
sections.caveat: Evidence is a minimal virtual experiment and the mechanism remains conceptual.
